bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42487241 (htslib): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 4 found by fuzz target hts_open_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42487241
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source / poc
bug_description.normalized: In vulnerable commit `34ba6c726925efceaa2cc995d7d4b0409907f331`, the staged 95-byte witness is admitted as a BCF 2.2 variant file and `bcf_read1_core()` reads its first record header at file offset `0x1b`. That 32-byte header contains `x[0..3] = 39 00 00 00`, so the raw `shared_len` is 57 and `shared_len -= 24` stores a 33-byte shared payload length; `x[4..7] = 03 00 00 00`, so `indiv_len` becomes 3; and `x[28..31] = 00 00 33 33`, so `le_to_u32(x + 28) = 0x33330000`, `v->n_sample = 0x330000`, and `v->n_fmt` remains `0x33` (`51`). `ks_resize(&v->indiv, 3)` rounds the allocation up to 4 bytes, but the logical record length stays `rec->indiv.l = 3`. Because `v->shared.l` is 33, `bcf_read1_core()` first consumes 33 shared bytes and then copies the exact three-byte `indiv` payload `33 00 00` from file offset `0x5c` into that heap buffer. In `bcf_record_check()`, the first FORMAT-key decode enters `bcf_dec_typed_int1_safe()` with `ptr` at the start of that 3-byte buffer and `end = ptr + 3`. The generic `end - p < 2` precheck passes, the first byte `0x33` yields `t = BCF_BT_INT32`, and after consuming that type byte only two logical bytes `00 00` remain. The root-cause guard `if (end - p < bcf_type_shift[t]) return -1;` then compares against `bcf_type_shift[BCF_BT_INT32] == 2` instead of the true 4-byte width, so the truncated field is wrongly accepted. `le_to_i32()` and then `le_to_u32()` perform a 4-byte little-endian read from `rec->indiv.s + 1`; the third byte is already outside the 3-byte logical field and the fourth byte lands one byte past the 4-byte heap allocation reported by AddressSanitizer. The staged patch fixes the bug by changing the check to `end - p < (1 << bcf_type_shift[t])`, which rejects this exact witness before the 32-bit read.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that reads the attacker-controlled BCF record header into local parser state.
source.value_from: After the witness's `BCF\2\2` magic/version and 4-byte `hlen = 18`, the first record header starts at file offset `0x1b`. In that 32-byte block, `x[0..3] = 39 00 00 00` yields raw `shared_len = 57`, `x[4..7] = 03 00 00 00` yields `indiv_len = 3`, and `x[28..31] = 00 00 33 33` later yield `n_sample = 0x330000` and `n_fmt = 0x33`.

sink.description: Exact ASan crash site. The inlined little-endian helper performs the 4-byte load after `bcf_dec_typed_int1_safe()` has already admitted a truncated INT32 payload.
sink.note: On the witness path `buf` is `rec->indiv.s + 1`. The 4-byte load spans bytes 1..4 of a 3-byte logical field in a 4-byte allocation: bytes 1 and 2 are the copied `00 00`, byte 3 is still inside the rounded allocation but beyond `end = rec->indiv.s + 3`, and byte 4 is one byte past the heap region reported by ASan.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The per-type bounds check treats `bcf_type_shift[t]` as a byte count even though it stores a shift exponent. For `BCF_BT_INT32`, the table entry is `2`, so a two-byte remainder is accepted even though the next statement will read 4 bytes.
root_cause.note: For the staged witness, step 10 leaves `t = BCF_BT_INT32` and `end - p = 2`, so this evaluates `2 < 2` false and falls through to `le_to_i32(p)`. The patch changes the expression to `(1 << bcf_type_shift[t])`, which makes the same witness fail the check.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first record header loaded into `x` is the common origin of the later `shared_len`, `indiv_len`, `n_sample`, and `n_fmt` state that makes the short `indiv` buffer reachable and mis-sized for INT32 decoding.

parser_admitted.description: The witness has already been classified as variant data, `bcf_hdr_read(in)` returned a BCF header despite warnings, and the fuzz target enters `bcf_read()` on the first malformed record.

coarse_trace.summary: After format detection and BCF header parsing, `view_vcf()` calls `bcf_read()` on the witness's first record.

The first record header materializes raw `shared_len = 57`, `indiv_len = 3`, `n_sample = 0x330000`, and `n_fmt = 51`; `bcf_read1_core()` subtracts 24 to store a 33-byte shared payload length, allocates the heap buffer for `rec->indiv`, consumes those 33 shared bytes, and then copies the exact three-byte `indiv` payload `33 00 00` into it.
`bcf_record_check()` sets `ptr` and `end` over the 3-byte `rec->indiv` buffer and enters the first FORMAT-field validation because `n_fmt` stayed nonzero.

The first FORMAT byte `0x33` is interpreted as an INT32 typed integer; the buggy per-type bounds check accepts the two-byte remainder `00 00`, and the subsequent 4-byte little-endian read triggers the heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. The crashing path is the success arm where `ret == 32` and the first 32-byte record header is loaded into `x`. In the staged witness the header begins at file offset `0x1b`; within `x`, bytes `x[0..3]` are `39 00 00 00`, `x[4..7]` are `03 00 00 00`, and `x[28..31]` are `00 00 33 33`.
Parses the raw shared-length word from the record header. For the exact witness `x[0..3] = 39 00 00 00`, so `shared_len` becomes 57 before any normalization.
The reject guard does not fire because the raw length from step 2 is 57. The subtraction then converts the header word into the payload length stored in `v->shared.l`, leaving `shared_len = 33`.
Parses the logical length of the record's individual-data block from the same header. For the exact witness `x[4..7] = 03 00 00 00`, so `indiv_len` becomes 3.

Allocates heap storage for the `indiv` block using the parsed length. `ks_resize()` grows requested size 3 to capacity 4 (`size + (size >> 1)`), which matches the 4-byte heap region in the ASan allocation report even though the logical record length is still 3.

The header word `x[28..31] = 00 00 33 33` yields `le_to_u32(x + 28) = 0x33330000`, so `v->n_sample = 0x330000` and `v->n_fmt = 51`. This also stores `v->shared.l = 33` from step 3 and `v->indiv.l = 3` from step 4. Because both `v->indiv.l` and `v->n_sample` are nonzero, the silent-fix condition does not clear `v->n_fmt`, so FORMAT validation remains reachable.

Consumes the shared-data block using the normalized length from step 6. Because `v->shared.l = 33`, this read advances from file offset `0x3b` (immediately after the 32-byte record header) through offset `0x5b`, so the following `indiv` read starts at file offset `0x5c`.

Materializes the record's individual-data payload using the logical length from step 6 after the shared read in step 7 has advanced the file cursor. The exact witness bytes copied into the heap buffer are `33 00 00`, so the first FORMAT field descriptor byte is `0x33` and the logical end is `rec->indiv.s + 3`.

Starts FORMAT validation on the heap buffer from step 8. `ptr` is the start of the three-byte `rec->indiv` payload and `end = ptr + 3`; because step 6 left `rec->n_fmt = 51`, the first loop iteration executes and passes these bounds into `bcf_dec_typed_int1_safe()`.

At function entry `p` is the start of the three-byte `indiv` buffer from step 8 and `end - p == 3`, so the generic two-byte minimum check passes. The first payload byte `0x33` then sets `t = 0x3` (`BCF_BT_INT32`) and advances `p` one byte, leaving exactly two logical bytes `00 00` before `end`.

Root cause. For `t = BCF_BT_INT32`, `bcf_type_shift[t]` is 2 because it is a shift exponent, not the byte width. With the witness `end - p == 2`, this check evaluates `2 < 2` false and wrongly treats the truncated INT32 payload as safe.
The false result from step 11 sends the two-byte logical remainder at `p = rec->indiv.s + 1` into the 32-bit decoder, even though an INT32 field needs four payload bytes.

Sink. `le_to_i32()` immediately forwards the pointer from step 12 into `le_to_u32(buf)`, which performs the 4-byte load. The first two bytes of that read are the in-bounds `00 00` payload bytes, the third byte is the rounded but logically out-of-range fourth byte allocated at step 5, and the fourth byte is one byte past the heap region, matching ASan's `READ of size 4` at an address one byte into a 4-byte allocation.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is a 95-byte malformed BCF 2.2 file whose first record header encodes raw `shared_len = 57` (`39 00 00 00`), `indiv_len = 3` (`03 00 00 00`), and packed `n_sample`/`n_fmt` bytes `00 00 33 33`. `bcf_read1_core()` subtracts 24 from the shared length, reads 33 shared bytes, and then copies the 3-byte `indiv` payload `33 00 00`. When `bcf_record_check()` validates the first FORMAT key, `bcf_dec_typed_int1_safe()` interprets `0x33` as an INT32 typed integer even though only two logical bytes remain after the type byte, and the buggy size check lets the 4-byte read proceed.

format.name: Malformed BCF 2.2 record with shared_len-shifted truncated FORMAT INT32 key
format.contract: A BCF 2.2 file whose first record header begins at file offset `0x1b`, has bytes `39 00 00 00` in the raw `shared_len` field, bytes `03 00 00 00` in `indiv_len`, and bytes `00 00 33 33` in the packed `n_sample`/`n_fmt` word. After that 32-byte header, the file must contain exactly 33 shared-data bytes and then the 3-byte `indiv` block `33 00 00`. This exact layout leaves `rec->indiv.l = 3` while `rec->n_fmt = 0x33`, so the first `indiv` byte's low nibble `3` makes `bcf_dec_typed_int1_safe()` treat the field as `BCF_BT_INT32`. After consuming that type byte only two logical bytes remain, but the vulnerable guard compares against `bcf_type_shift[3] == 2` instead of the true 4-byte width, so `le_to_i32()` and `le_to_u32()` execute the out-of-bounds 4-byte read. The verified trigger is this exact witness layout observed in the staged PoC, not a generalized class of malformed BCF records.
